sections.content: How many people are "shopkeepers and owners - retail and wholesale"?

132,690 people

were counted on the census as "shopkeepers and owners - retail and wholesale" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Shopkeepers and proprietors in this unit group direct and carry out activities in the running of small, independent retail and wholesale establishments.

People who had this job were generally older

The occupation of "shopkeepers and owners - retail and wholesale" had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 55 to 59 years. Of the whole working population 10.4% were aged 55 to 59 years. For people working as "shopkeepers and owners - retail and wholesale", 14.1% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "shopkeepers and owners - retail and wholesale" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "shopkeepers and owners - retail and wholesale" included:

  • sewing machinists
  • education advisers and school inspectors
  • undertakers, mortuary and crematorium assistants

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "shopkeepers and owners - retail and wholesale" there were more men than women (57.3% compared with 42.7%).

This means "shopkeepers and owners - retail and wholesale" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "sales occupations".

Men made up 57.3% and women made up 42.7% of "shopkeepers and owners - retail and wholesale"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women. This occupation was one of the jobs for which the proportion of men and women was closest to this overall picture.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "shopkeepers and owners - retail and wholesale" included:

  • quality assurance technicians
  • sports coaches, instructors and officials
  • ambulance staff (excluding paramedics)

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "shopkeepers and owners - retail and wholesale" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "shopkeepers and owners - retail and wholesale" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "shopkeepers and owners - retail and wholesale", 14.3% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (60.6% compared with 39.4%).

They are also more likely to be self-employed (84.3%) than an employee (15.7%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
